prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Move sign-in after pet adoption [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +15.0%, measured +3.6% ± 1.7%, after noise correction +2.7%, won
- round 1: Interactive tip carousel on waiting screen [home, redesign]: predicted +8.0%, measured -4.2% ± 2.1%, after noise correction -2.8%, lost: worse
- round 1: Desktop display shortcut hint on final intro screen [finish, hint]: predicted +12.0%, measured -3.2% ± 3.4%, after noise correction -1.4%, lost: no clear effect

By kind of change, after noise correction:
- finish, hint: -1.4% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, redesign: -2.8% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: +2.7% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

One test is weak evidence. State a rule only when at least 2 tests of that kind agree after noise correction; otherwise say the evidence is still thin.

Previous lessons:
(none yet)

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Evidence is still thin for sign_in reorder, home redesign, and finish hint changes because each kind of change has only one test so far.
Predictions were consistently too high across all tested changes.
